Data processing addendum

How Loadout Labs processes personal data for customers who use Loadline. It forms part of the Loadline terms.

Version 1.0, effective November 4, 2026

This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") forms part of the end user terms under which a customer uses the Loadline app for Jira Cloud ("Loadline"), provided by Loadout Labs LLC, 4030 Wake Forest Rd Ste 349, Raleigh, NC 27609, USA ("Loadout Labs", "we"). Those end user terms are Atlassian's standard end user agreement for Marketplace apps with Loadline's Provider-Specific Terms, which name this DPA under the agreement's Section 3.3. It applies when the customer ("Customer", "you") installs Loadline on an Atlassian site and Loadline processes Customer Personal Data. If this DPA and the end user terms conflict on the processing of personal data, this DPA wins.

1. Definitions

  • Data Protection Laws: the laws that apply to the processing of Customer Personal Data under this DPA, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 ("GDPR"), the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection, and the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended ("CCPA"), each as applicable.
  • Customer Personal Data: personal data that Loadline processes on the Customer's behalf, as described in Annex 1.
  • Atlassian: Atlassian, which hosts and runs Loadline on its Forge platform (see Annex 3).
  • Controller, Processor, Data Subject, Personal Data Breach, Processing, Sub-processor: as defined in the GDPR.

2. Roles

The Customer is the controller (or a processor acting for its own controller) of Customer Personal Data. Loadout Labs is a processor (and, under the CCPA, a service provider) that processes it only to provide Loadline.

3. How Loadline is built, and what that means for this DPA

Loadline is an Atlassian Forge app that "Runs on Atlassian":

  • All of its code runs on Atlassian's cloud infrastructure, and all of its data is kept in Atlassian-hosted storage (Forge SQL), in a separate database for each Atlassian site.
  • Loadline sends no data outside Atlassian. It has no egress: it calls no Loadout Labs server or other service.
  • Loadout Labs has no access to any site's Loadline data. We cannot read, export or change it. Our access is limited to deploying new versions of the app and reading the app's operational logs, which hold counts and run identifiers, never personal data.

Because of this, several obligations below are met by the platform's design or by Atlassian, and the clauses say so.

4. Processing on instructions

We process Customer Personal Data only to provide Loadline as described in its documentation and the end user terms, which together are the Customer's documented instructions. The Customer's Jira site administrators give further instructions through Loadline's settings (for example, what Loadline imports and who may approve decisions). We will tell the Customer if we believe an instruction breaks Data Protection Laws.

5. Confidentiality and security

  • Anyone at Loadout Labs who works on Loadline is bound by confidentiality.
  • We maintain the technical and organisational measures in Annex 2, and Atlassian maintains the platform measures it describes for Forge. We may update the measures if the protection they give is not reduced.

6. Sub-processors

  • The Customer authorises the Sub-processor in Annex 3.
  • We will give at least 30 days' notice of a new Sub-processor by updating this page and the Loadline listing. The Customer may object on reasonable data protection grounds within that time; if we cannot address the objection, the Customer may uninstall Loadline and end the subscription as its only remedy, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the unused period where the end user terms allow.
  • We remain responsible for our Sub-processors' processing of Customer Personal Data as Data Protection Laws require.

7. Helping the Customer

  • Data Subject requests: Customer Personal Data is held on the Customer's own site, so the Customer's Jira site administrators can find, correct and delete it with Loadline's admin page and with Jira itself. When an Atlassian account is closed, Loadline erases that account's identifier and name automatically, through Atlassian's personal data reporting. If a request needs more, we will help as far as we reasonably can, given that we cannot see the data.
  • Impact assessments and consultations: we will give the Customer the information about Loadline it reasonably needs, such as this DPA and Loadline's privacy and security answers.

8. Where data is processed

  • Customer Personal Data stays in Atlassian-hosted storage and follows the data residency of the Customer's Atlassian site, including when Atlassian moves the site to another region.
  • Loadout Labs does not receive or store Customer Personal Data, so we make no transfers of it ourselves.
  • Standard Contractual Clauses are therefore not part of this DPA. If a Customer's own assessment requires them, or if Loadline ever starts sending Customer Personal Data outside Atlassian, we will agree suitable transfer terms with the Customer (for example, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum, with Annexes 1 to 3 of this DPA as their annexes) before any transfer happens.

9. Personal data breaches

We will tell the Customer without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours, after we become aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Customer Personal Data, including one reported to us by Atlassian. We will give the information we have and reasonably can get to help the Customer meet its own obligations, and we will take reasonable steps to contain it. We fix security vulnerabilities in Loadline within the time limits of Atlassian's Security Bug Fix Policy for Marketplace apps.

10. Deletion

  • While Loadline is installed, data is kept as described in Annex 1 (for example, daily plan snapshots for 90 days).
  • When the Customer uninstalls Loadline, Atlassian deletes the app's storage for that site. Atlassian may keep it for up to 28 days in case the site asks for it to be recovered. Loadout Labs holds no copy.
  • If a subscription lapses without uninstalling, the data is kept so that subscribing again restores it; the Customer can uninstall to delete it.

11. Audits

Because Loadout Labs cannot access Customer Personal Data, audits are met by information: on request, we will provide this DPA, Loadline's privacy and security answers, a summary of our most recent security review, and written answers to reasonable questions, no more than once a year unless a supervisory authority requires it or after a Personal Data Breach. Atlassian's platform certifications and reports cover the hosting (see Annex 3).

12. CCPA

As a service provider, Loadout Labs will not sell or share Customer Personal Data, will not retain, use or disclose it for any purpose other than providing Loadline, and will not combine it with other personal data.

13. Liability, term and law

  • Each party's liability under this DPA is subject to the limits in the end user terms.
  • This DPA lasts as long as Loadline processes Customer Personal Data.
  • This DPA is governed by the law and courts set in the Provider-Specific Terms (North Carolina, USA), except where Data Protection Laws require otherwise.

Annex 2: Technical and organisational measures

  • Hosting: Loadline runs on Atlassian Forge and keeps its data in Atlassian-hosted Forge SQL, one isolated database per site, encrypted at rest and in transit by the platform.
  • No egress: Loadline makes no calls outside Atlassian; it is eligible for Atlassian's Runs on Atlassian program.
  • No vendor access: Loadout Labs cannot read, export or change any site's data.
  • Access control: every page function and Rovo action runs as the person using it and shows only work in Jira projects they can browse; admin settings require Jira administrator permission; decision approval is limited to named approvers, with Jira administrators as the fallback.
  • Least privilege: five Atlassian scopes: four read-only, plus report:personal-data for personal data reporting. No write access to Jira.
  • Testing: automated tests, including a permanent test that checks a restricted viewer never sees hidden work, run before every release; dependencies are checked for known vulnerabilities before every release.
  • Logging: operational logs hold counts and run identifiers, never personal data or credentials.
  • Personal data lifecycle: weekly reporting of stored Atlassian accounts, automatic erasure of closed accounts and refresh of changed names.
  • Vulnerability handling: reports to security@loadoutlabshq.com; fixes within the time limits of Atlassian's Security Bug Fix Policy for Marketplace apps.
